newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks close sharply off.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks close sharply off.

text.p: Mexican stocks fell for the seventh session in a row Monday as investors avoided the risks of Mexico's political and social problems to join the bullish U.S. stock market.
"Political and social concerns are overriding the economic situation which, without exaggerating, is satisfactory," said Roberto Solano, deputy research director at the Estrategia Bursatil brokerage.
"I think uncertainty has increased due to the prospect of confrontation prior to the (mid-term congressional) elections in 1997."

The blue chip IPC index closed down 41.64 points, or 1.27 percent, at 3,246.65. In the broader market, 103 stocks changed hands, of which losers well outnumbered gainers by 61 to 19 on light volume of 56.4 million shares.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 76.03 points, or 1.12 percent, at another record close of 6,547.79.

"We broke an important support at 3,250 points, after which dealers continued to sell a little," Solano said. "We see a stronger support at 3,200 points, where there may be some opportunities to buy," he added.

Financial stock GFInver headed the gainers' list, up four centavos (1 cent) at 68 centavos (9 cents). Traders noted the stock had been favourably priced as GFInver will be taken over by Spanish bank Santander.
Debt-ridden holding company Sidek headed the losers, down 15 centavos (2 cents) to 1.00 peso (13 cents).
